The relationship between transformational leadership behaviors and healthcare workers' sleep quality appears to have a mediated role. Transformational leaders are expected to promote high levels of self-efficacy among their team members. Self-efficacy is the individual's belief in their ability to execute tasks and achieve goals. In this context, transformational leaders may encourage healthcare workers to develop skills necessary for effective leadership, which in turn enhances their self-efficacy.

Studies suggest that training managers in transformational leadership behaviors can positively impact healthcare workers' health over time. However, more research is needed to uncover the specific mechanisms by which transformational leadership leads to improved sleep quality among healthcare workers.

In other words, while transformational leadership behaviors may directly contribute to higher levels of self-efficacy, this relationship with sleep quality requires further investigation. More studies are necessary to explore how the impact of these behaviors on sleep outcomes can be elucidated.

Therefore, it is essential to continue researching this topic to gain a deeper understanding of the complex relationships between transformational leadership, self-efficacy, and healthcare workers' sleep quality.
